responseText: {"title":"Lines That Cannot Stay Inside","question":"When marks escape the face's boundary, what is left of the face?","introduction":"Fifteen works share a single pressure: lines that refuse to stay within the face they describe. Some push outward in hard diagonals; others dissolve the boundary until figure and field are nearly the same thing. This exhibition follows that pressure from faces still holding their shape, through works where overflow becomes the main event, to images where recognition hangs by the thinnest visible thread.","closing":"Each work asks the same question differently. Where the boundary holds, the face survives. Where it does not, something else takes its place — and the gallery leaves that something unnamed.","chapters":[{"title":"The Face Still Holds","introduction":"Four works where a recognizable face dominates the canvas, even as lines press hard against its edges and begin to leak past them.","stops":[{"slot":"W003","whyHere":"Pointed ears, rectangular eye zones, and bared teeth lock the face in place; scribbled loops spilling into the teal ground are the first sign of pressure building outward.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W075","whyHere":"A thick black scaffold holds the rectangular head firm against saturated red; the zigzag crown and triangular teeth read as almost orderly, yet crossing lines flood every interior surface.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W003 leaks loosely into open teal, W075 is hemmed by a hard yellow border — the pressure is the same but the container is tighter."},{"slot":"W094","whyHere":"Squared eye-frames and a wide tooth-filled mouth give the face a mask-like flatness; teal outline loops extending into the red field signal that the boundary is already giving way.","transitionFromPrevious":"W075 holds its shape through thick black scaffolding; W094 replaces that scaffold with flat framing squares, and the red field pressing in from outside feels more aggressive."},{"slot":"W076","whyHere":"A rigid cyan-and-white outline holds a near-square head against dark navy; magenta ring-eyes pull attention inward while ribbon lines spill into all four corners.","transitionFromPrevious":"W094's red field pushes inward; W076 reverses the pressure — the dark navy recedes and the face's own lines are what escape outward into the corners."}]},{"title":"The Overflow Becomes the Event","introduction":"Five works where the lines escaping the face are as visually dominant as the face itself — boundary and field competing on equal terms.","stops":[{"slot":"W035","whyHere":"Mismatched eye heights and a striped mouth anchor the face, but the spiky scribble field pressing inward from every edge competes with the features for the viewer's attention.","transitionFromPrevious":"W076's overflow stays ribbon-like and peripheral; in W035 the scribble mass is dense enough to crowd the face from all sides simultaneously."},{"slot":"W038","whyHere":"Red X marks inside heavily cross-hatched oval eyes and a grimace-wide tooth band hold the center, while colored lines spill past the face edge into a jagged, unclosed border.","transitionFromPrevious":"W035's scribble field presses inward; W038's lines press outward — the direction reverses, but the face is equally contested in both."},{"slot":"W011","whyHere":"Hard diagonal wedges shoot to every image edge, breaking the face into shards; the two small rectangular eye zones are the only still point in a composition that pulls entirely outward.","transitionFromPrevious":"W038 retains a closed face shape with leaking edges; W011 abandons closure — the diagonals dominate and the face is reconstructed from what remains."},{"slot":"W025","whyHere":"Looping yellow lines spread like unraveling wire across the upper half while the stacked-block face below holds firm; the hot-pink field and the cool layered shapes at right pull in opposite directions.","transitionFromPrevious":"W011's overflow is sharp and angular; W025 replaces hard wedges with looping wire — the energy is the same but the texture shifts from shards to coils."},{"slot":"W089","whyHere":"Magenta loops and black scribbles refuse every boundary, spilling into all four corners; the single squared eye and red-arced mouth are the only features that hold their position inside the density.","transitionFromPrevious":"W025 keeps a firm block-face anchoring the lower half; W089 offers only one squared eye and a mouth arc — the face is already thinning."}]},{"title":"Accumulation Without Outline","introduction":"Three works where the face emerges from density rather than drawn edges — features readable only because marks pile up more thickly in some places than others.","stops":[{"slot":"W073","whyHere":"Layer after layer of short scribble lines accumulate until the face is a site of density; two small eye forms are the only fixed points inside the surrounding noise.","transitionFromPrevious":"W089's face still has a legible arc-mouth and squared eye; W073 reduces those anchors to two small dark forms nearly swallowed by the scribble mass."},{"slot":"W128","whyHere":"The face is built entirely from looping lines with no solid fills; features emerge only where loops compress most tightly, and the background's own dense scrawl pushes the face forward without a hard edge.","transitionFromPrevious":"W073's scribble lines are short and directional; W128 replaces them with long looping coils — the face becomes even less outlined and more accumulated."},{"slot":"W057","whyHere":"Pale radiating spikes dissolve the head's boundary into the warm looping background; the tooth-filled mouth is the one hard-edged anchor left in a composition where figure and field share the same line weight.","transitionFromPrevious":"W128 holds the face forward through background contrast; W057 removes that contrast — face and ground use identical line weight, and the boundary nearly disappears."}]},{"title":"The Grid Holds What the Face Cannot","introduction":"Three works that impose a structural grid or rectangular frame over the dissolving face — testing whether geometry can recover what the overflow has taken.","stops":[{"slot":"W107","whyHere":"Four quadrants divide the composition like a grid, but the dividing lines bulge and overlap; the two mismatched spiked circles and barred rectangles suggest face-parts arranged rather than drawn.","transitionFromPrevious":"W057 dissolves the face through shared line weight; W107 tries to reassemble it through a grid — but the grid itself refuses to stay tidy."},{"slot":"W129","whyHere":"A tilted rectangular form locks a face-like structure inside a crossing-line grid; spiral eye forms anchor the composition while every other layer — bars, loops, hatching — presses inward around them.","transitionFromPrevious":"W107's grid is divided into four equal zones; W129 tilts the whole structure, making the grid feel less like a container and more like another layer of pressure."},{"slot":"W133","whyHere":"Strict rectangular framing — two boxed spiral eyes, one long zigzag-mouth box — holds the composition together even as cyan, yellow, red, and black lines fill every zone including the background with no empty space.","transitionFromPrevious":"W129's grid competes with the marks it contains; W133 makes the rectangles the dominant visual fact, the last structural claim the face can make on a fully saturated field."}]}]}
